extracted.intended_audience: contributors to mathlib / authors of Lean library files
extracted.subtask_description: A style guide for writing and organizing Lean (mathlib) source files covering naming, layout, docstrings, proofs, tactic usage, API design, deprecation, and performance practices for contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use conventional names for variable categories (e.g., u,v,w for universes; α,β,γ for generic types; a,b,c for propositions; x,y,z for elements; h,h₁ for assumptions; p,q,r for predicates/relations; s,t for lists or sets; m,n,k for naturals; i,j,k for integers). Types with mathematical content use usual mathematical notation (G for group, R for ring, K or 𝕜 for field, E for vector space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention may not hold in older files where greek letters are used for all types; pull requests renaming type variables in those files are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unicode usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use special Unicode characters, especially mathematical symbols, where they help notation and readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid characters which change text direction, invisible characters (except spaces and newlines), and characters which modify other characters. Mathlib has a linter checking characters against an allow-list; new characters may be added as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line length
rubrics_metrics.description: Lines should not be longer than 100 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps files easier to read, especially on small screens. VS Code has a visual marker for the 100 character limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Header and imports formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: File header should contain copyright info, a list of all authors who made significant contributions, and a description of contents. Put the module keyword on its own line after the header, skip a line, then group all public imports together, skip another line, then group all imports. Try to keep imports alphabetical within each block.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Authors' even for a single author; don't end the line with a period; separate author names with commas (no 'and'). Less common combinations like `public meta import` or `import all` exist but their relative location is not prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Module docstring contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a module docstring (delimited with /-! and -/) after the header and imports containing a title, a summary of contents (main definitions/theorems/proof techniques), notation used, and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a 'Main results' section listing key declarations, a 'Notation' section, and a 'References' section. New bibliography entries should go into docs/references.bib. If the docstring lines wrap, indent subsequent lines by two spaces (markdown requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Top-level declarations flush-left
rubrics_metrics.description: All declarations (def, lemma, theorem, class, structure, inductive, instance, etc.) and commands (variable, open, section, namespace, notation, etc.) are considered top-level and should appear flush-left; opening a namespace or section does not indent its contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This holds for declarations starting with def, lemma and theorem. In VS Code hovering shows fully qualified names even when namespace is open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing around punctuation and operators
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spaces on both sides of ':', ':=' and infix operators. Put them before a line break rather than at the beginning of the next line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent spacing improves readability and avoids awkward line breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'indent' to mean indent by 2 additional spaces unless otherwise specified. After stating the theorem, indent lines in the subsequent proof by 2 spaces. If the theorem statement requires multiple lines, indent subsequent statement lines by 4 spaces while the proof remains indented 2 spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for nat_case and le_induction show exact indentation levels. When a term spans multiple lines, indent each continuation by an additional two spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't orphan parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep parentheses with their arguments; do not leave opening or closing parentheses orphaned on separate lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examples in the guide demonstrating how to place parentheses in multi-line terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit types for arguments and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of all arguments of a declaration should be given explicitly, and the return type of declarations should also be given (Lean enforces this for theorems).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes definitions easier to understand when viewed on web pages (e.g., GitHub). Example contrasts BadStatement (implicit types) vs GoodStatement (explicit types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short declarations on a single line
rubrics_metrics.description: A short declaration can be written on a single line (e.g., trivial theorems or short defs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: theorem succ_pos : ∀ n : Nat, 0 < succ n := zero_lt_succ; def square (x : Nat) : Nat := x * x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of 'by' for tactic mode
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing a proof in tactic mode, place 'by' on the line prior to the first tactic; do not place 'by' on a line by itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice you will often see ':= by' at the end of a theorem statement. Everything within the tactic block is indented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting of 'have' justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A have can be put on a single line when the justification is short; when the justification is too long, put it on the next line indented by an additional two spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the justification of the have uses tactic mode, the 'by' should be placed on the same line, regardless of whether the justification spans multiple lines. Examples show both forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line-breaking arguments and multi-argument proof terms
rubrics_metrics.description: When a proof term takes multiple arguments, it is sometimes clearer to put some of the arguments on subsequent lines; indent each additional argument (i.e., indent an additional two spaces per continuation line).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies whenever a term spans multiple lines; examples illustrate how to align arguments for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class and structure field formatting and docstrings
rubrics_metrics.description: In class or structure definitions, fields are indented 2 spaces, and each field should have a docstring (/-- -/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show docstrings for fields like top and down'. Use 'where' and 'extends' appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructor arguments alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: When using a constructor taking several arguments in a definition, arguments should line up (align vertically).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: theorem Ordinal.sub_eq_zero_iff_le shows how constructor arguments are lined up for readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances: prefer 'where' syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing terms of structures or instances of classes, prefer the 'where' syntax to avoid enclosing braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reusing an existing instance 'instBot', use '__ := instBot' to forward fields; examples show instance instOrderBot : OrderBot ℕ where bot := 0 bot_le := Nat.zero_le and the shorthand with __.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses placement (left of colon preferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally prefer having arguments to the left of the colon rather than using universal quantifiers or implications if the proof starts by introducing these variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prefer 'example (n : ℝ) (h : 1 < n) : 0 < n := by linarith' over a curried formulation. Note: pattern-matching is an exception where hypothesis right of the colon is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Binders formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a space after binders and generally write binder types explicitly even if Lean can infer them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: '∀ α : Type, ∀ x : α, ∃ y : α, y = x := fun (α : Type) (x : α) ↦ Exists.intro x rfl'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous functions and lambda syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer 'fun x => ...' or the ↦ arrow for anonymous functions; the lambda notation 'λ x ↦ ...' is disallowed in mathlib in favor of 'fun'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The pretty printer displays ↦; use 'fun' as the mathlib default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculational proof ('calc') style
rubrics_metrics.description: Place 'calc' on the line prior to the calculation and indent the calculation. Align whichever relations are involved across lines; leave '_' placeholders left-justified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justifications don't need to align ':=' symbols but it can help. Several example styles are provided: full-explicit, interchangeable-lines style (preferred for editing), and compact style for short expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactic-mode conventions and mixing with term mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Place 'by' before tactic blocks and indent tactics; focus new goals with the dot '·' (not indented); mixing tactic and term mode is allowed. Use named subgoals with 'refine' and 'case' when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often use one tactic per line; short sequences corresponding to a single idea can be on one line separated by semicolons. Examples include multi-goal strategies, cases x <;> simp [a,b,c,d], and examples of short one-line tactic proofs using 'by tac1; tac2;'. Use 'swap' or 'pick_goal' to close very short goals immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'case' for named subgoals
rubrics_metrics.description: When tactics create named subgoals (e.g., via refine), use 'case' to prove them in whichever order is desired, improving readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows refine ⟨?imp, ?converse⟩ followed by 'case converse =>' and 'case imp =>'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Squeezing 'simp' calls discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminal simp calls should not be replaced by their squeezed output (the output of simp?), unless performance requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: (1) squeezed calls can be longer and drown important information about key lemmas; (2) they refer to many lemmas by name and are fragile to lemma renamings. Avoid using the output of simp? to replace calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profiling for performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should be aware of performance impacts and benchmark changes (use '!bench' on a PR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PR touches significant components (adding classes, instances, simp lemmas, changing imports, creating new definitions, or turning defs into abbrevs), benchmark proactively. Nontrivial refactor PRs should be benchmarked and any significant negative results explained in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency levels and API design
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand transparency levels: reducible (always unfolded), semireducible (default; usually not unfolded), and irreducible (never unfolded unless requested). Def by default creates semireducible; abbrev creates reducible and @[inline] definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer semireducible unless a documented reason exists. Consider how exposing underlying terms affects instance search/simplification; authors may need to declare instances with inferInstanceAs and provide API lemmas for simp use. For sealed API boundaries, prefer a structure wrapper (with an 'underlying' field) over irreducible. Use irreducible_def only when kernel-level blocking is necessary and documented. Use of 'erw' or extra 'rfl' after tactics operating at reducible transparency indicates missing API — consider adding API lemmas. PRs that remove transparency abuses must benchmark and explain consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitespace and delimiter preferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Lean is whitespace-sensitive; prefer avoiding explicit delimiting with ';' unless necessary. Prefer '<|' over '$' and use '|>' as appropriate to avoid parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prefer 'f <| by ...' instead of 'f (by ...)', and use 'foo a |>.bar b |>.baz' for chained dot notation. When using rw or simp, put a space after the left-arrow '←' (e.g., rw [← add_comm a b]). Also ensure a space between tactic name and its arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empty lines inside declarations discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Empty lines inside declarations are discouraged and enforced by a linter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comments to explain code rather than empty lines; a short sentence communicates more than an empty line in a proof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Settle on one standard 'normal form' for equivalent statements and use it in statements and conclusions; register simp lemmas to convert other forms to the normal form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: prefer s.Nonempty and (a : Option α) as normal forms. Special cases: for bottom/top element assumptions prefer hne (x ≠ ⊥) in assumptions and hlt (⊥ < x) in conclusions because conversions are asymmetric and one direction is easier to check/use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use /-! -/ for module doc delimiters and section headers (they become auto-generated docs), /- -/ for technical comments or implementation notes, '--' for short/in-line comments, and /-- -/ for documentation strings for declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a docstring spans multiple lines, do not indent subsequent lines. See documentation requirements for more suggestions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting expressions in error/trace messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Inside printed messages, names and interpolated data should either be inline and surrounded by backticks or on their own line and indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces clearer output. Example: m!"{foo} must have type {bar}" or indent with indentD for multi-line messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deprecation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly exposed theorems and definitions that are being removed should be gracefully transitioned using the @[deprecated] attribute with a 'since' date and either an alias to the new declaration or a string message explaining migration. Renamed definitions should use a deprecated alias to the new name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: to_additive deprecations should ensure proper tagging. Deprecated declarations can be deleted after 6 months. The 'deprecate to' command and scripts/add_deprecations.sh can help generate aliases. Simultaneous renaming of X→Y and W→X is allowed but discouraged; in that case no deprecation is required for X but is required for W.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid nonrec where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid the nonrec keyword when the apparently recursive calls conflict with another declaration in a namespace; prefer adding the namespace to that declaration instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If it conflicts with a declaration in the root namespace, both nonrec and _root_.[...] are acceptable. Avoiding nonrec may require forgoing dot notation in the body. There are legacy places that break this rule.
